metadata.title: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Martha Kahn [11. Dezember 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.70

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Martha Kahn [11. Dezember 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.70
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.70
- Datum: 11.12.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Rio, 11.12.40
Dear Martha, It is a long time since I want to address
you again a few personal words, only there is usually a rush
on the days where letters have to be posted-and first of all written.
I very much hope that you are well and I even suppose
that for you the removal to another flat together with Smolletts
is rather welcome than otherwise. I can imagine that nearly
as lively as „Rosemount“, even if there are few visitors.
That Lotte is representing you in Bath I know and I hope she
likes being there as much as you and I loved it. But where
is Raethe now, could she continue work in that children's
home at Uxbridge? And did you get any good news about
the girls' brother? I do hope you did. I often think of our
house how it is now, without you, without Eva, without us and
on hot days I remember the wintry afternoons when we came
up from the town and gathered round the fire. I don't know
whether I am getting old, but I certainly got sentimental about
Bath and the years in Woodstock Road. The house in Woodstock
Road seems over now, but I hope that one day we will all
unite again in „Rosemount“. - In the meantime we are braving
the heat which is slowly developping, and I have even de-
cided to go and bathe in the sea to-morrow morning at
8! (later it gets too hot). We intend to remain here another
month and then hope to go to the States for a few winter
months. I am looking forward to seeing ~~eva~~ Eva who seems
to be so busy going to parties that she has to be reminded
of letter-writing.
With the best wishes for the New Year
Dear Martha, Lotte as a worthy aunt of Eva has left Lotte.
this letter a good fortnight on her desk and so it arrives after
Christmas and Newyear. When shall we meet again. I am longing
after the „Heimstätte Marthas“ and an own room with my books
and not more to see luggage, visas, railways for some time. Yours Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig auf gelblichem Papier. Die letzte Zeile 'Lotte.' ist eine handschriftliche Ergänzung von Lotte Zweig.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift von Stefan Zweig ist klar. Die Ergänzung von Lotte Zweig am Ende ist ebenfalls gut lesbar.
